evidence.note: Claim CONFIRMED: perf_metrics.detect_* (6 knobs) are consumed by core/perfdetect.py as cfg.detect_* but invisible to test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs.dead_knobs() because cfg is the PerfMetricsConfig section, not Config().perf_metrics. Probe: worktree .venv/bin/python -c 'import test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs as t; print([k for k in t.dead_knobs() if k.startswith("perf_metrics.")])' printed the 6 detect_* knobs (dead) before the fix and [] after adding section-qualified reads in _section_knobs.

Read governing rules via ddflow claim note + brief: r-task-phase-needs-wave (item carries phase bugs-2, needs no-deps, wave:0), r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY before gemini review), r-small-files, r-adapters. No rule forbids the _section_knobs anchor read; it extends the existing dead-knob linter anchor pattern.

Extended _section_knobs in ddflow/services/perf/store.py to name all nine [perf_metrics] knobs (3 ring + 6 detect_*) as section-qualified reads so the dead-knob linter sees perfdetect's detect_* consumption; Store.__init__ now assigns self.perf_metrics = perf_metrics or _section_knobs(Config()).

chunk_findings.detail: `Store.__init__` always executes `_section_knobs(Config())` and discards the result, even when the caller already passed a `perf_metrics` section. Previously `_section_knobs` ran only in the `perf_metrics or …` fallback, so an injected config never touched the process config. Given `Store(repo, perf_metrics=explicit_cfg)` in an environment where `Config()` cannot load (missing file, bad env, test sandbox), line 343 raises and construction fails even though `explicit_cfg` is valid and would have been assigned to `self.perf_metrics`.

chunk_findings.detail: The stated failure is that a name-based knob scan treats `perf_metrics.detect_*` as dead because perfdetect reads those knobs unqualified. This edit does not change perfdetect and does not add any qualified name that was not already a load: `ring_max_bytes`, `ring_max_age_s`, `aggregate_min_samples`, and every `detect_*` attribute were already referenced as `config.perf_metrics.<knob>` and the function already returned `config.perf_metrics`. Binding the same loads to `_` and returning a prior `section` alias is invisible to that scan. Given perfdetect source that mentions `detect_min_samples` (and the other `detect_*` knobs) without a `perf_metrics.` prefix, `test_no_knob_is_dead` still fails exactly as before B61962d45e0.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/store.py:316

chunk_findings.detail: The bug-fix task requires a regression test that fails on the unfixed code and is what closes B61962d45e0. The whole change is only this store.py rewrite, so nothing asserts the qualified `detect_*` names stay live. A later edit that drops the tuple (or leaves perfdetect unqualified) ships with the same dead-knob failure and no test to catch it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/store.py:314

data.summary: When a task is added to a phase that is already done (e.g. P-drivers marked done 18/18, then DRV-delta-from-descriptor filed into it), the phase stays done while holding an open task, so it reads "done 18/19" — a live inconsistency. A phase that reports done must have zero open tasks. Fix: task add / bug found (--phase <done-phase>) and a task becoming open under a done phase must re-open the phase and invalidate its completion, so the phase pipeline (unit_tests/merge gates) re-runs; a truly-closed phase must refuse a new open task unless the operator explicitly re-opens it.
data.title: a done phase can hold an open task (done 18/19), and filing a task into a done phase does not re-open it

A phase that reports done must have zero open tasks. Fix: task add / bug found (--phase <done-phase>) and a task becoming open under a done phase must re-open the phase and invalidate its completion, so the phase pipeline (unit_tests/merge gates) re-runs; a truly-closed phase must refuse a new open task unless the operator explicitly re-opens it.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B86e99de0c6 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B86e99de0c6 --regression-test <test>` first).
